newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong gold edges up on shortcovering.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong gold edges up on shortcovering.

text.p: Hong Kong gold firmed on Wednesday on shortcovering and some speculative buying once European markets opened but traded volumes remained thin, gold traders said.
"We saw some speculative buying from London," said one gold source.

He noted that the U.S. Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) decision on Tuesday to leave interest rates unchanged may have spurred players to buy the yellow metal while gold prices remained favorable.
The market also saw some shortcovering, traders said, noting however that players had gotten used to selling as the market dropped and were still slightly hesitant to buy on the upside.
Traded volumes thinned as the market looked for direction, they said.
Germany has said it remains opposed to gold sales by the International Monetary Fund (IMF), noting it has alternative financing plans to aid developing countries.
One trader suggested that gold may be hit by political uncertainty in Russia, where security head Alexander Lebed said on Wednesday that unpaid armed forces may go on the rampage.
Bullion ended at US$383.00/383.50 an ounce Wednesday against New York's US$382.60/383.10 close on Tuesday.
Local gold ended HK$12 higher at HK$3,529 a tael.
The carry over charge at the Chinese Gold and Silver Exchange Society remained unchanged from its Tuesday fix at -6.
